result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.get_similar_neighbors()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Get neighbors with similar attribute values. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L5249-L5373){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.get_similar_neighbors( node, node_attr, tol_abs=None, tol_pct=None, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Returns neighbors whose numeric attribute values fall within a specified tolerance range of the starting node's value. Useful for finding connected nodes with comparable properties. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [node]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Union[int, str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Starting node ID or label to compare against. [node_attr]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Name of the numeric attribute to compare. [tol_abs]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [tuple[float, float] | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Absolute tolerance as `(lower_bound, upper_bound)` from the starting value. For example, `(1.0, 2.0)` means values from `start_value - 1.0` to `start_value + 2.0` are considered similar. [tol_pct]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [tuple[float, float] | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Percentage tolerance as `(lower_pct, upper_pct)` from the starting value. For example, `(10, 20)` means values from `start_value × 0.9` to `start_value × 1.2` are considered similar. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [list[int]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : List of neighbor node IDs with similar attribute values. Empty list if the starting node lacks the attribute or has no neighbors in range. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the attribute exists but is not numeric (int or float). ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} When neither `tol_abs` nor `tol_pct` is set, similarity collapses to strict equality on the attribute value, so only exact matches come back. With `tol_abs=t` a neighbor $v$ of $u$ counts as similar when $|x_v - x_u| \le t$, and with `tol_pct=p` the tolerance rescales with the anchor as $|x_v - x_u| \le p \cdot |x_u|$, which is what you want when the attribute spans several orders of magnitude. Neighbors that lack the attribute simply drop out of the result; a non-numeric attribute raises `ValueError` rather than silently misbehaving. ## Examples {.doc-examples} Only "B" falls within ±1.0 of "A"'s value of `5.0`; "C" at `10.0` is far outside that range: ::: {#fb5be069 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph() graph.add_node("A", value=5.0) graph.add_node("B", value=5.5) graph.add_node("C", value=10.0) graph.add_edge("A", "B") graph.add_edge("A", "C") similar = graph.get_similar_neighbors("A", "value", tol_abs=(1.0, 1.0)) [graph.get_label_from_id(nid) for nid in similar] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` ['B'] ``` ::: ::: Percentage tolerance scales with the starting value instead of using a fixed range -- here ±20% of `5.0` covers `4.0` to `6.0`, which still excludes "C": ::: {#a4bee7db .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_node(label="A", value=5.0) .add_node(label="B", value=4.5) .add_node(label="C", value=10.0) .add_edge(source="A", target="B") .add_edge(source="A", target="C") ) similar_pct = graph.get_similar_neighbors("A", "value", tol_pct=(20, 20)) [graph.get_label_from_id(nid) for nid in similar_pct] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` ['B'] ``` ::: :::
